title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: infection/reatus; prefer corruption tip before Isaiah
pass_a_gloss: You then prop the reply with queries: how else explain this infection and guilt? Why did Adam's fall ruin and doom to death not a lone person but human nature as a whole, when other men's actual sins only wound persons and make themselves death-guilty? How is an actual sin justly laid on us that we never did, ordered, urged, or willed, and that was involuntary for us? Can you answer those? Better, then, to hold fast the spread of inborn corruption and the guilt that follows—Scripture teaching it, experience confirming it—and leave the ungrasped mode to God, than to mint, beside and against Scripture, an imputation still harder to grasp that twists and soils divine justice.
pass_b_english: For the rest, you shore up this answer of yours with questions. For, you say, who can otherwise give the reason of this infection and guilt? Why, I ask, did Adam by sinning destroy and subject to death not only a person but also the whole human nature—whereas other men by their actual sins wound persons and make themselves liable to death? How can an actual sin be justly imputed to us which we ourselves neither did, nor ordered, nor advised, nor approved by any consent of our will, and which with respect to us was in no way voluntary? Can you give the reason of these things? Would it not then be better firmly to believe the propagation of inherent corruption and of the guilt which follows it—Scripture teaching, experience bearing witness—and to leave to God the mode which you do not grasp, than beside and against Scripture to invent an imputation equally, or more, hard to grasp, and one that perverts and stains the justice of God?
source_text: Caeterum hanc tuam responsionem interrogationibus firmas. Nam, inquis, qui potest aliter reddi ratio hujus infectionis & reatus? cur quaeso Adam peccando perdidit, & morti subjecit, non tantum personam, sed etiam totam naturam humanam? Cum caeteri homines peccatis suis actualibus laedant personas, & se mortis reos efficiant. Qui potest nobis peccatum actuale juste imputari, quod neque fecimus ipsi, neque jussimus, neque suasimus, neque ullo voluntatis nostrae consensu probavimus, quodque nostro respectu nullo modo voluntarium fuit? Horumne tu rationem reddere potes? Annon igitur satius esset propagationem corruptionis inhaerentis & reatus qui eam sequitur, docente Scriptura, contestante experientia, firmiter credere; modum autem quem non capis Deo permittere, quam praeter & contra Scripturam imputationem excogitare aeque, aut magis difficilem captu, ac Dei justitiam pervertentem, & maculantem?

choices.choice: Prefer Scripture corruption-propagation over invented imputation; stop before Isaiah 55
